assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling turned aryl amination into a general, predictable tool; it is ubiquitous in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis and rests on clear mechanistic and ligand-design insight. Impact is broad, original and lasting, and it is a natural complement to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic systems and ligand families that made the reaction practical. Kosugi's early tin-amide work is a genuine precursor but not the decisive step for general utility; the prize could acknowledge it only by a three-way split.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, many independent confirmations and industrial scale adoption; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Precedence of Kosugi and the Migita/Kosugi tin chemistry versus the Buchwald and Hartwig generalization may draw debate
Overlap with the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize could be seen as incremental
My recollection of exact priority dates is from memory and not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation (PROTACs and molecular glues) created a new therapeutic modality in which small molecules recruit E3 ligases to remove proteins, with a conceptual shift in drug discovery and many compounds in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others made important later contributions, so credit is broad and any trio leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Concept validated by many independent groups and clinical-stage degraders; first approvals have not clearly arrived, so there is some timing risk.
uncertainties: Clinical proof (approved drugs) is still maturing
Relative weight of PROTAC versus molecular glue lineages is unresolved
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto, Ciulli and Handa is contestable

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites transformed photovoltaics research, with efficiencies rising from a few percent to above 25% in a decade, and opened a materials family with wide chemistry and optoelectronic relevance. The impact on solid-state and materials chemistry is large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported the perovskite sensitized cell, Park made the solid-state cell and Snaith the thin-film solid-state device, but Kanatzidis, Grätzel and Seok also made key contributions. Any three-person configuration is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation of efficiency, but long-term stability and commercial viability are unresolved, which argues for some patience.
uncertainties: Device stability and lead toxicity may make the recognition look premature
Disputed credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing allows direct chemical conversion of one base to another in genomic DNA without double-strand breaks, a genuine invention of molecular chemistry with therapeutic consequences and broad adoption. Chemical logic of engineered deaminase fusions is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: David Liu led the concept and the work; Komor (cytosine) and Gaudelli (adenine) made the first-generation editors as lead researchers. Nishida and Kondo have a parallel cytosine deaminase report, which complicates priority. Liu alone would be the cleanest choice, but I list the trio to reflect the two base-editor classes.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are underway and independent replication is extensive; the field is recent and the CRISPR prize in 2020 already recognized genome editing, so timing is plausible but not urgent.
uncertainties: Fit with the 2020 CRISPR prize and whether the Chemistry committee views this as sufficiently distinct
Whether young co-inventors should be named alongside Liu
Prime editing (a separate candidate) may be bundled by some members

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pores, organic structure-directing agents and defined active sites underpins refining, emissions control and fine-chemical catalysis. The field is close to my own area, so I weigh it knowing of that closeness; the science is important and the impact is lasting and industrial.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalyst design, structure-property relations), Davis (new framework types and shape-selective catalysis) and Zones (SSZ zeolites and SDAs for Chevron) are decisive, but Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis also made notable advances. The candidate is broad and may be fragmented between synthesis and catalysis.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and industrial deployment; recognition would be timely or somewhat late. The topic is mature.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed across many groups and the discovery is a compound field rather than a single event
Whether the committee sees zeolite catalysis as closely related to the 2025 MOF prize and thus already covered
My closeness to the porous materials field could bias my assessment

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic structure and ionic motion, enabling ab initio simulation of liquids, solids and reactions. It is a foundational method of computational chemistry, widely used, with clear originality and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is a clean two-person attribution with no serious dispute; the credited names fit a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and numerous independent implementations; recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Computational chemistry was recognized in 2013 and 2024, and the committee may feel it has already rewarded this area
Parrinello is also credited in other candidates, so the Committee may prefer a different framing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate noncanonical amino acids at designated sites through orthogonal tRNA synthetase pairs, creating a general chemical-biology platform for protein engineering and for new biologics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the first orthogonal pair strategy and amino-acid incorporation in vivo; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms, quadruplet codons and genome-recoded cells; Yokoyama contributed key synthetase engineering and structural work. Wang and Mehl are also important, so a three-person configuration omits significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for two decades; the genome-recoding frontier is newer.
uncertainties: Close conceptual and technical relation to the 2018 evolution prize and 2024 protein design prize may be argued against
Allocation among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama is unresolved

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from micro- and nanocrystals and time-resolved studies of reactions, which complements electron diffraction for crystals too small for conventional X-ray work. It has been demonstrated on photosystems, enzymes and photoactive proteins.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the first demonstration and the method framework, Fromme and Hajdu provided early crystal and concept contributions, and Schlichting was a leader in time-resolved applications. Spence and others, not on the supplied credit list, are also cited in the field, so the allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The method is demonstrated and used worldwide, though access to XFEL facilities is limited and most impact so far is on a modest number of systems; timing is plausible but not pressing.
uncertainties: Limited number of landmark structures with fundamentally new chemistry so far
Credit allocation among Chapman, Fromme, Hajdu and Schlichting, and others not credited
I am a structural method specialist in a neighbouring technique, so I rely on recollection of the XFEL literature
